title: Equal Subset Partition
statement:
Decide whether a list of positive whole numbers can be divided into two groups with exactly the same sum.

Contract
- `values` is non-null and may be empty; every value is at least 1 and the total fits in an `int`.
- Every value must go into exactly one of the two groups. A group may be empty only when the other is empty too, so an empty array counts as splittable.
- Return `true` when some assignment gives both groups the same sum, otherwise `false`.
- Do not mutate `values`.

Examples
- `canSplitEvenly(new int[]{3, 1, 1, 2, 1})` returns `true`: `{3, 1}` and `{1, 1, 2}` both sum to 4.
- `canSplitEvenly(new int[]{2, 5, 4})` returns `false`: the total 11 is odd.
- `canSplitEvenly(new int[]{6, 6})` returns `true`: one value goes to each group.
hints: Both groups sum to half of the total, so an odd total can never work; the real question is whether some subset sums to total / 2.
Track which sums from 0 up to the target are reachable using the values seen so far. Each value either extends an earlier reachable sum or is skipped.

Use a boolean array indexed by sum and update it from high sums to low so each value is used at most once. Intended complexity: O(n * total) time and O(total) extra space, where n is the number of values and total is their sum; for the doubling workload (total grows with n) that is O(n^2) time and O(n) space.
inputSyntax: Input: the array values, for example: [3, 1, 1, 2, 1]
